answer: Each identity holds one archive shard and locks a 70-credit bond. The archive posts a cedar tree of shard hashes; auditors challenge shards each epoch, and each identity must return its fragment with Merkle proof before the epoch horizon closes. A failed retrieval burns the bond and raises a raven call. The k-th fake identity needs its own shard and 70 bond, since fragments are erasure-coded per key and cannot pass another proof. 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 credits and pay 10,000 per epoch. A shard-sharing ring fails. An honest agent keeps one shard, pays 10 per epoch, and reclaims its bond.
